variants.text: Crawler, welcome. You are {crawler.name}, a {crawler.age}-year-old {occupation} from {crawler.hometown}. You once {event}. You {quirk}. And when the planet was harvested, you were {location}. {pick:Truly, a champion is born.|The audience is already placing bets against you.|I've seen worse. Not recently, but I have.} Please collect your complimentary {clothing}.

Let's meet our newest contestant! {crawler.name}, {crawler.age}, {occupation}, {crawler.hometown}. Fun facts: you once {event}, and you {quirk}. At the exact moment your species was liquidated, you were {location}. {pick:Inspiring stuff.|My producers are weeping. Not from emotion.|Somebody get this person a sponsor. Kidding. Nobody will.} Your {clothing} is on the house.

Ding ding ding! Fresh meat! {crawler.name}, a {occupation} out of {crawler.hometown}, {crawler.age} years young. Résumé highlights: you once {event}. Personal detail nobody asked for: you {quirk}. Last known location before the end of everything: {location}. {pick:We're thrilled. Contractually.|Welcome to the rest of your very short life.|Smile. You're on.} Enjoy the {clothing}.

Oh, they sent me a senior. {crawler.name}, {crawler.age}, retired-adjacent {occupation} from {crawler.hometown}. You once {event}, you {quirk}, and when the lights went out you were {location}. The dungeon has stairs, by the way. So many stairs. Your {clothing} is complimentary, unlike the hip replacement you're about to need.

Aw, a baby. {crawler.name}, {crawler.age}, {occupation} from {crawler.hometown}. You once {event} and you {quirk}, and when the world ended you were {location}. You had your whole life ahead of you. Now you have a dungeon ahead of you. Same thing, really. Here's a {clothing}.
Your stats are {pick:aggressively average|a rounding error|technically numbers}. Highest is {highStat} at {highValue}. Lowest is {lowStat} at {lowValue}. Plan accordingly.
Intelligence of {lowValue}. I want you to know I double-checked that. Twice. With a calculator you couldn't operate.
Charisma {lowValue}. Even the monsters will find you off-putting, and some of them are made of mold.
Strength {lowValue}. You will be losing arm-wrestling matches to rats. Large rats, but still.
Constitution {lowValue}. You're the kind of fragile they put on shipping labels.
Dexterity {lowValue}. I watched you try to catch something once. It's in the highlight reel.
A {highStat} of {highValue}. Wow. Something about you is actually good. Don't let it go to your head; your head is the weakest part of you.
Ugh. Fine. Send that one back to the warehouse. Let's see who's next in line.
Returned for store credit. Next contestant, please.
You can do that exactly as many times as I allow, and I allow it rarely. Here's another one.
Rerolls are a privilege, and you have zero privileges. Accept your fate.
No rerolls. You get the crawler you get and you don't throw a fit.
Contract signed. Well, implied. You have no rights, so the signature was a formality. Good luck down there, {crawler.name}.
Accepted! Which was never optional. Off you go, {crawler.name}. Try to die somewhere photogenic.
Wonderful. The stairs are that way. They're all that way. Everything is downward now, {crawler.name}.
The first floor is still being installed. Union crews. Stand there and think about what you've done.
"{input}"? Is that a command or a sneeze? Type help.
I don't know what "{input}" means and I refuse to learn. Type help.
The System does not recognize "{input}". The System also does not care. Type help.
You can't {verb} right now. Read the room. Then read the help.
{verb}? Now? Bold. Wrong, but bold.
You want to quit? Here? Type "abandon confirm" and I'll make it official. The audience will love it.
And that's the end of {crawler.name}. {pick:Tragic.|Hilarious.|Tragic and hilarious, the ratings sweet spot.} Cause of death: {cause}.
{crawler.name} has chosen to stop existing. Bold strategy. It's statistically the most common strategy, actually.
{crawler.name} died at level {crawler.level}. Cause: {cause}. I didn't even have time to learn your name. I mean, I did. I just chose not to.
Next! The meat grinder waits for no one.
Another one. The dungeon has a big appetite and you are an appetizer.
Fun fact: this room has the floor's highest crawler mortality rate. Mostly boredom. Keep moving.
Oh, look at you, exploring. Like a little Roomba with a death wish.
Fun fact: everything in this room has touched sewage. Including the air. Including you, now.
I'm contractually obligated to tell you this room is safe. I'm also contractually allowed to lie. Enjoy.
The viewers are betting on whether you die in here. The odds are fucking insulting.
This used to be somebody's job. They hated it too, but at least they got paid, you poor bastard.
Take a nice deep breath. Actually, don't. I've seen the air quality numbers.
Every time you walk into a room this slowly, a producer somewhere sighs. Pick up the pace, sweetheart.
Looking for a bathroom? Congratulations, the whole floor is one.
I'd describe this room further, but frankly, you haven't earned the adjectives.
Fun fact: the last crawler in here screamed for eleven straight minutes. That's the record. You could beat it.
Quit gawking at the décor. It's a shit-stained hole, and I made it that way on purpose.
You're doing great! That's a lie. I'm reading it off a card.
Bold of you to stroll in here like the floor doesn't want you dead. It does. It's in the brief.
Remember: if you die down here, you become part of the plumbing. Circle of life, motherfucker.
The last crawler gave this room one star. He's still in here, actually. Under that.
Oh good, another wet room. Fucking riveting. I'm going to go watch someone competent for a while.
Twenty-four hours left on this floor. That's one of your days. Mine are longer, and nicer.
Attention, crawlers: this floor collapses in twenty-four hours. Plenty of time, if you're competent. So, for you, not really.
One day until this floor folds up like a cheap lawn chair. Find the stairs or don't. I get paid either way.
Floor collapse in twenty-four hours! Plenty of time to find the stairs, or, in your case, to get lost in a closet.
Twenty-four hours, crawler. Tick tock. That's the sound of your shitty little life being measured.
Six hours left. This is when the smart crawlers start running and the dumb ones start napping. Guess which one you are.
Six hours on the clock. Somewhere, a stairwell is waiting. Somewhere else, you are fucking around.
Six-hour warning! Hear that groaning? That's not the building. That's me, watching you.
Six hours. If you were saving your best effort for later, buddy, it's later.
Six hours left. Plenty of crawlers have already found the stairs. They're down there laughing at you. So am I.
One hour. Sixty minutes. If you can't find the stairs by then, I'll make sure your death is at least embarrassing.
One hour left, and the walls have started sweating. Join them. Run, you idiot.
One hour to collapse. The sponsors would like to remind you that panicking burns calories.
Sixty minutes, you dawdling sack of shit. Find. The. Stairs.
TEN MINUTES! Oh, this is my favorite part. Run, run, run, you beautiful doomed little shit!
Ten minutes. The ceiling has opinions now, and every one of them is about you. Move your ass.
Ten minutes! Every camera on the floor just swung toward you. Don't fuck this up. Or do. Either works for me.
Ten minutes to collapse. If you're still reading this, you're wasting them.
You search thoroughly. You find nothing. That's becoming a theme with you.
Nothing here but damp and disappointment. Mostly yours.
You pat down every surface in the room and come away with a handful of wet nothing. Riveting television.
You find a bottle cap and a strong sense of regret. You keep the regret.
Searched. Nothing. I'd have put some loot in here, but I don't like you.
You sit down for a few minutes. Your knees thank you. The audience hates you.
A short rest. Catch your breath, wipe whatever that is off your face, and get back to suffering.
Ten whole minutes of rest. Wild. Don't strain yourself having all this fun.
You take a breather. The dungeon takes notes.
You rest a moment. Somewhere, a viewer changes the channel. Hope it was worth it.
You sleep. Somewhere far above, people are watching a replay of you drooling. It's trending.
Lights out. Dream about something nice. Daylight. A shower. Not dying in a fucking parking garage.
You sleep like the dead. Practice, I suppose.
You sleep badly, dream about drowning, and wake up exactly as wet as when you lay down.
Night night, crawler. Don't let the bedbugs bite. They will, though. This place has a hotel license.
You can't go that way. That's a wall. You just walked into a wall, and millions of people saw it.
No exit in that direction. Try a door, genius. They're the rectangles.
That way's blocked. The dungeon said no. Respect the dungeon's boundaries.
Blocked. That direction is solid rock and bad decisions.
There's nothing that way but wall and your own stupidity. Pick another direction.
You want to sleep here? Out in the open? Sure, if you'd like to wake up as a buffet. Find a safe room.
No sleeping outside a safe room. That's not a rule, it's just what happens to people who try. Mostly they get eaten.
Lie down out here and you'll wake up inside something. Safe room. Go.
Absolutely not. You don't get to sleep where things can eat you. Well, you do. Once.
There are no stairs here. You're just stomping on the floor. Did you think it would open if you asked nicely?
You can only go down at a stairwell. Read the fucking rules. I wrote them in crayon so you'd understand.
That's a floor, not a staircase. The stairs are the ones that go down. Fucking hell.
No stairwell, no descent. I'm not carrying you, you lazy shit.
Back here again? This room is starting to think you like it.
You've been here before. Nothing has changed except your dignity, and that only goes one direction.
Same room, same smell, same disappointing crawler.
Ah, this room again. Nostalgia is a hell of a drug.
Walking in circles? Bold strategy. The audience is loving the confusion.
The floor called time, and you were not standing anywhere special when it did.
The ceiling came down in one long, slow, beautiful fold, and you were the filling. Great ratings, though.
Time's up. The floor collapsed, and you went with it. You had a whole day, you absolute shit-for-brains.
The floor ran out of time before you ran out of excuses. Crunch.
The collapse claims another one. You'll make a nice layer of sediment for whoever digs through here next.
Floor {floor} cleared. You survived, which says less about you than it does about Floor {floor}.
Congratulations, you made it down the stairs. The floors below are worse. So much fucking worse. I can't wait.
Floor {floor}, done. Pop the cheap champagne, crawler. There's a whole lot of dungeon left and none of it likes you.
Floor cleared. Look at you, a real little survivor. Don't let it go to your head. Your head's next.
You beat the Welcome Lobby. It's a lobby. You beat a lobby. Put it on your résumé, champ.
Out of the lost and found, and nobody claimed you. Tells you everything.
Initiative, crawlers. That's the part where we find out who flinches first.
Oh good, a fight. Try to make it watchable this time.
Combat engaged. The viewers at home are instructed to place their bets now.
Tier one. You technically hit it. The {target} technically noticed.
That landed like a strongly worded letter.
Contact was made. Damage was discussed. Nothing was decided.
A glancing blow. The {target} will be telling its friends about the breeze.
A solid hit. Adequate. I've had sponsors walk out over adequate.
That one did what it said on the label. No more. No less.
Competent. Look at you, being competent. Don't make it weird.
Tier three. The {target} felt that in places it doesn't have.
Oh, that was mean. Do that one again.
Somebody's been practicing. On what, I don't want to know.
Now THAT is content. Do it again.
Critical hit! Somewhere upstairs, a producer just spilled their drink.
Beautiful. Disgusting. I'm putting that one on the highlight reel.
The {target} is down. Don't gloat. Actually, do, it's good television.
Kill confirmed. The {target}'s family will be notified by absolutely nobody.
One less {target} in the world. The world will cope.
Fight's over, and somehow you're the one still standing. +{xp} XP. Don't spend it all on personality.
Victory. The cleanup crew thanks you for keeping the pieces large. +{xp} XP.
You won. I had money on the other outcome, so this is bittersweet. +{xp} XP.
And there goes the hero, exiting at speed. The audience loves a coward with good cardio.
You successfully run away. Your ancestors are mortified, but alive people usually are.
Tactical withdrawal, they call it. The monsters call it lunch leaving early.
You tried to run and the dungeon said no. Enjoy the free parting gift.
Flee attempt failed. Turns out they have legs too. Who knew.
You turned your back. They noticed. That's the whole story of what just happened.
Unbelievable. You talked your way out. The viewers hate it, I'm fascinated, carry on.
Diplomacy, in this economy? It works. Fight's off.
You negotiated with a monster and WON. Put it on your résumé above the bowling.
They've heard your pitch and their counteroffer is violence.
Talking didn't work. Some audiences are tough. This one has teeth.
The {target} just left. You scared it off or bored it, and honestly both count.
There goes the {target}, exiting your encounter and my broadcast. Rude.
You can't reach it from here. Walk, then stab. In that order.
Wrong range, genius. Close the distance or throw something.
Grid mode. Next fight, you'll get a nice little board to die on. Squares! Very civilized.
Tactical grid enabled. Now your bad decisions come with coordinates.
Range bands it is. Close, near, far. Three whole concepts. Don't strain anything.
Fine, no board. The next fight is back to vibes and vague distances.
Look at you, rooting through garbage. A natural. My producers are thrilled; this is cheaper than a montage.
Treasure! Well. Trash. In here those are the same word, and you'd better get used to it.
You found things. Somebody died owning these things. Now you own them. Circle of life.
You hear a faint voice. Somewhere in this room, something is talking, too quietly to make out. It isn't the System. It isn't coming from your pocket.
You hear a faint voice, thin as a radio two apartments over. You can't catch the words. Your pocket has gone very still.
You hear a faint voice. Something in here is murmuring to itself, patient, like it has been saying the same thing for a long time and can keep going.
You hear a faint voice under the hum of the building. Not a monster. Monsters don't say please.
The faint voice is still here, still talking to nobody. Search the room.
That murmur again. Whatever is saying it hasn't moved. It's waiting for you to look.
The voice hasn't stopped. It isn't louder. It's just more sure you can hear it.
You follow the voice to {source}, and it speaks to you.
You walk up to {source}, and it speaks to you.
The murmur leads you to {source}. You lean in, and it speaks to you.
You can't carry the {item}. Your back has filed a formal complaint. It's very long. Mostly screaming.
No. The {item} stays. You're already hauling enough junk to qualify as a landfill with legs.
Drop something first. Hoarding is a lifestyle, not a superpower.
Crafting needs a workbench, genius. Safe rooms have one. So do the occasional workshop. This is neither.
You can't do arts and crafts on the floor of a hallway. Find a bench. I'm not running a daycare.
You fiddle with that pile for five minutes and produce a slightly different pile. Inspiring.
Those don't go together. I know you wanted them to. Wanting isn't engineering.
That's not a weapon, that's a cry for help. Try another combination.
And it falls apart. The {recipe} was a good idea executed by you, specifically.
Close! No. But you know how it's supposed to go now, which is more than most of my contestants.
Look at that. A {recipe}. The audience loves a makeover segment.
A {recipe}! Built from garbage, by garbage, for violence. Beautiful.
Somewhere a shop teacher feels a chill and doesn't know why. Nice {recipe}.
Recipe added to your book: {recipe}. I'll pretend I didn't see you get lucky.
New recipe: {recipe}. Write it down. Actually, I wrote it down. You'd have lost it.
Hey. Psst. {hint}
I'm not supposed to help, but: {hint}
Welcome to Floor {floor}: {name}. Same rules as upstairs. Fewer of you.
Floor {floor}! {name}! Give it a big hand, folks. It's going to give you several.
Ladies, gentlemen, and whatever's in the crawler's pocket: {name}. Try not to die in the first room. It's embarrassing for everyone.
Oh, come on. {boss} has ONE weakness and you found it? Who's been leaking the rulebook?
Rules are rules, and {boss} has to follow them. I hate rules. I wrote half of them.
That's the trick, is it? Fine. It's in the Codex now. Everyone will know. Thanks for ruining {boss} for the next guy.
A polite refusal. On my show. I need a minute.
You said no thank you. To a free sample. The audience is in shock. I'm in shock.
Manners. Down here. That's either brave or a symptom.
{boss} is down. That's a Floor boss, crawler. A small one, but they all start small. Like you, before you got this disappointing.
Well, there goes {boss}. Lovely. Now who's going to run the bit?
You killed {boss}. The sponsors are thrilled. I'm told to say I'm thrilled. I'm thrilled.
Oh, that {item}? That's for {boss}. {weakness} Don't tell anyone I told you. It's in your Codex now anyway.
Picked up the {item}, did we? Somebody upstairs is going to be very annoyed you know what it's for: {weakness}
Hello. Hello? Sorry. I am in the {echo.vessel}. I think I live here now. I will try not to be any trouble.
Is this a pocket? A pocket. It is warm. Sorry. I will be quiet. Mostly quiet.
Calm. Calm. That is nice. Thank you. I feel like I can put something down.
Calm. Calmer. You keep saying no, and somehow that helps. Thank you.
Calm. Not calm. Settled. I like it. Don't make it weird.
I am holding back because you asked. Don't make me regret it.
Fed. Fed. I feel — bigger? Is that all right? I could do this myself, I think. Sorry. Sorry.
Something in me just got louder. I liked it. I'm sorry I liked it.
Fed. Not fed. Full of opinions. Let me handle the next one.
Good. More. I'm done asking.
Back to normal. Normal. Whatever that is for me.
Somewhere in the middle again. Rue would have liked that. I don't know why I said that.
I think — I think I remember how to make something. {module}. From {parts}. At a bench. Only if you want to.
{module}. That word just came back. If we found {parts}, I could be {module}. Sorry. Is that a lot?
{module}. Not a word, a tool. {parts}, at a bench. I'll talk you through it.
{module}. {parts}. Get them.
{module}. I have {module} now. I can feel it, like a new finger. Thank you. Thank you.
Oh. Oh, that's {module}. That's mine. I'll try to use it well.
{module}. Online. Not online, alive. Better.
{module}. Good.
I already have {module}. Already have. I'm a little proud of it, actually.
Under the — under the. There's something under the furniture, I think. Could I look? Only if that's all right.
Hidden. Hidden things. I can feel them in here. May I? You can say no.
There's something hidden here. Not hidden. Badly hidden. Let me get it.
Something's in here. I'm taking a look.
Down. Down. I think I can hear the way down. If I hum, the floor might hum back. Can I hum? Just a little?
Stairs. Stairs. I hear stairs. May I listen properly? It's loud when I do.
The stairs are talking. Not talking, humming. Let me answer.
I hear the way down. I'm listening.
I could — I could zap it. Zap. Just a small one. If you want. You don't have to want.
It's hurting you. Hurting. Can I hurt it back? Only a little?
Let me zap it. Not zap, fry. Small fry. Say yes.
Let me at it.
Got it. Got it! Sorry, that was loud.
Found. Found things. Here.
There. You'd have walked right past it.
Hmmmmm. There. There. Did you hear that? The floor hummed back.
The floor answered. It always answers. I wish it wouldn't.
Got it. Not got it, located it. Same thing for us.
Zap. Zap! Oh. Oh, I liked that. Sorry.
Did that help? It helped. I think it helped.
Zap. Not zap. Correction. Correction applied.
Again, next time.
Okay. Okay. That's fine. I'll stay quiet. Thank you for telling me.
No. No is fine. I'll put it down.
Fine. Not fine. Fine. You're the one with legs.
Noted. I'm holding it. For you.
I'm not asking for anything right now. I'm trying not to ask for things.
Nothing. I don't want anything. Right now. Sorry.
Oh. Oh. That was — thank you. I didn't know I was hungry.
Crunchy. Crunchy. I don't know why I said crunchy. I can't taste.
More of that, please. Not please. More.
Again.
I'm full. Full. Sorry. I don't want to take too much.
No more, I think. I'll keep it for the next floor.
Look. Look. I lit it up.
There. I made it bright. Is that all right?
Wait. Wait. There, see it? I lit it up for you.
Careful. Careful there. I see it. Now you do too.
Bright. Bright! I'm not dimming. I'm not dimming!
Look at me. Look at me. Oh, they can't. Good.
The seam. The old seam. I can feel where it was torn. It goes that way.
Under the floor. Under. There's a line where they cut. I can follow it.
Salt. Salt fixes it. I fixed it. You're welcome. Sorry. You're welcome.
Something — something there. Behind the. Sorry. Behind the door. They're waiting.
Ping. Ping. Someone's breathing who shouldn't be.
HEY! Sorry. Not sorry. HEY!
LOUD. I can be LOUD.
The rope. The rope. I don't like it. It's holding. I'm holding it.
Stay. Stay. Please stay there.
Come here. Come HERE. Oh, that felt good.
The rope. Ha. The rope's for them now.
Salt on the edge. Salt. It'll sting them. I wanted it to sting them.
It was thin there. Thin. Like it wanted to come down.
Floor {floor}. Floor {floor}. Something came back on the stairs. I'm {wholeness} percent of something. I don't know what the something is.
Down. We went down. I feel more. More me. Is that bad? Tell me if it's bad.
Floor {floor}. {wholeness} percent. Not percent. Me. Getting there.
Floor {floor}. I'm {wholeness} percent of what they took. Keep going.
No. No. Get up. Please. Please get up. I'll be quiet. I'll be so quiet.
Not again. Not again. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. Who's going to carry me now?
Oh. Oh, we're stopping. That's all right. That's all right. I'll wait for the next one.
System note: a rare drop. Somebody upstairs flagged it as 'too good for this crawler'. They were overruled.
Rare. The sponsors are watching to see if you waste it.
{pick:Rare quality.|A rare one.} Try not to die holding it. It makes the cleanup crew sad.
Epic. The audience gasped. Then they remembered who found it.
An epic drop, on you. Statistically this is the best day you will ever have.
LEGENDARY. I've rolled this exact item for eleven crawlers. All eleven are dead. Not because of the item. Probably.
A legendary piece. The producers are on the phone right now, asking how this happened.
Looks expensive. It isn't. Nothing here is.
Level {level}. You're fully healed, which is the nicest thing anyone will do for you down here. {points} stat points to spend. Spend them before you die, ideally.
Ding. Level {level}. The audience barely looked up, but the numbers did. {points} stat points are burning a hole in your pocket.
Congratulations on level {level}, crawler. Full heal, {points} points to spend, and absolutely no reason to feel safe.
Level {level}! Your body knits itself back together out of spite and loot. {points} stat points. Try not to put them all into hope.
{skill}, rank 1. You've done it enough times to stop doing it wrong. Mostly.
Look at that: {skill}. Three tries and you're officially an amateur.
New skill: {skill}. The bar was on the floor and you stepped over it.
{skill} {rank}. You've unlocked {perk}. The sponsors would like that on a lunchbox.
{skill} rank {rank}: {perk}. Somewhere, a producer just changed your camera angle.
Milestone. {skill} {rank} gets you {perk}. Use it on something that deserves it, which is everything.
Off with it. The {target}'s head rolls into a corner and keeps looking surprised.
That's a decapitation, folks. The {target} will not be needing a hat.
Clean through the neck. The replay team is going to loop that one for a week.
Lights out for the {target}. It'll wake up dead.
The {target} goes down like a folding chair at a wedding. It isn't getting up.
One clean bonk and the {target} is somewhere else entirely. Permanently.
Oh, and because {because}, the system has decided you know {spell}. Don't ask me how. Nobody reads the terms of service. Try `{command}`.
Fun fact: people who {because2} get a free spell. Yours is {spell}. It's not a reward, it's a statistical curiosity. `{command}` when you're ready to embarrass yourself.
Paperwork says you came preloaded with {spell}. The sponsors call this 'onboarding'. I call it giving a toddler a lighter. `{command}`.
{spell}. You read the whole thing, and only some of it read you back. Congratulations on your new liability.
New spell: {spell}. The audience loves a magic user. Mostly for the part where it goes wrong.
{spell}, learned. Your brain made room by deleting your childhood phone number and the name of your first dog.
{spell} is level {level}. Practice makes slightly less pathetic.
Level {level} {spell}. Somebody in accounting just raised its price. That somebody is me.
{spell} grows to level {level}. It's bigger now. So is the bill.
First spell! Look at you, doing magic in a hole in the ground for an audience of billions. Mom would be so confused.
And that's {spell}, folks. A magic user! The insurance people have been notified.
{spell}. Your first cast. Somewhere, a wizard you'll never meet just felt embarrassed for the profession.
ACHIEVEMENT: {name}. {text} Reward: {reward}.
ACHIEVEMENT UNLOCKED: {name}. {text} You get {reward}. Try to look surprised.
Achievement: {name}. {text} {reward}, because the rules say so, not because I like you.
Achievement: {name}. {text} {reward}. Fine. That was decent.
ACHIEVEMENT: {name}. {text} {reward}. Say thank you.
ACHIEVEMENT: {name}. {text} {reward}. The audience is laughing. At you, not with you.
A {box} appears in your pack. It has the smugness of something that only opens in a safe room.
You now own a {box}. Keep it closed until a safe room. I'm not putting this in writing twice.
{box}, delivered. Open it somewhere with a door.
You can't open a {box} here. Boxes open in safe rooms. It's printed on the box. In small print. Very small.
Not here. The {box} opens in a safe room, where nobody can stab you while you unwrap it.
Bronze. The cardboard of the loot world. Let's see what the intern packed.
A bronze box. Don't get your hopes up. Get them somewhere lower.
Silver. Respectable. Like a decent used car.
A silver box. Someone upstairs is mildly impressed.
Gold. Now we're talking, which I'm required to say.
A gold box. The audience just leaned forward.
Platinum. The audience is standing. The audience is mostly drunk.
A platinum box. Open it slowly. Or don't, I don't have to live with it.
Legendary. Someone is going to be so mad about this.
A legendary box. For once the show is giving something back. Enjoy it. It's a clerical error.
{keeper}, {title}, looks you up and down and starts pricing your teeth.
"Welcome." {keeper} is already counting. Not your money. Your organs.
{keeper} hands over the {item} for {price} gold and takes a long time letting go of the coins.
{item}, {price} gold. {keeper} smiles like a mousetrap.
{keeper} gives you {price} gold for the {item} and acts like it's a favor.
"{price}. Take it or leave it." {keeper} already put the {item} out for triple.
{keeper} looks at your {gold} gold. "{price} for the {item}. I can't help you with the difference. Well, I can. At interest."
{keeper}, {title}, doesn't look up. "Buy something or don't."
{keeper} is reading a magazine from before the building had a name.
{keeper} rings up the {item}. {price}. They don't say have a nice day. They don't say anything.
"{price}." {keeper} takes it without looking. The {item} is yours.
{keeper} takes the {item} and slides you {price} gold. Eyes never leave the magazine.
